examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Norm of a Vector in an Inner Product Space of Continuous Functions
examples.problem:
Let $V=\mathcal{C}\left[0,1\right]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $\left[0,1\right],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
\langle x(t),y(t) \rangle = \displaystyle\int_{0}^{1} x(t) y(t) \, \textrm{d}t.
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)= 2t-1.$
examples.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is defined as

$$
\| f(t)\| = \sqrt{\langle  f(t),  f(t) \rangle}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(f(t))^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(2t-1)^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(4{t}^{2}-4t+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={(\frac{4{t}^{3}}{3}-2{t}^{2}+t)|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}-2+1 \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\| f(t)\| = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{3}} = \dfrac{\sqrt 3}{3}.
$$

feedback.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(1)y(1)+x(0)y(0)+x(-1)y(-1).
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $p(t)=4-{t}^{2}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $p(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $p(t)=4-{t}^{2},$ we obtain

$$
p(1)=3,\,p(0)=4,\,p(-1)=3.
$$

Computing $‖p(t)‖$ using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖ & =\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩} \\  & =\sqrt{p(1)p(1)+p(0)p(0)+p(-1)p(-1)} \\  & =\sqrt{[p(1)]^{2}+[p(0)]^{2}+[p(-1)]^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(3)^{2}+(4)^{2}+(3)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9+16+9} \\  & =\sqrt{34}.\end{aligned}
$$
